UAE: For use in the UAE, establish what the receiving organisation needs and check UAE MOFA’s attestation instructions. Ask about any destination-side stage and translations before choosing a route.
Saudi Arabia: For Saudi Arabia, identify whether the request concerns employment, academic recognition or a technical trade. Check the receiving body’s instructions; do not assume every document follows the same consular route.
Qatar: For Qatar, obtain the requesting organisation’s checklist and confirm the competent consular route. The document category, purpose and any translation request matter.
Oman: For Oman, check Convention applicability as well as the recipient’s requirements. An authentication route does not settle recognition or translation requirements.
Bahrain: For Bahrain, check the relevant treaty relationship and the document’s scope. Confirm with the receiving institution before arranging additional legalization.
Kuwait: For Kuwait, ask the relevant embassy and recipient about the applicable authentication stages. Check whether the request is for the original, a copy or a translation.
UK: For the UK, establish whether the recipient needs authentication, direct issuer verification or a different form of evidence. Confirm Convention applicability where an apostille is requested.
Germany: For Germany, review relevant Convention declarations and the German recipient’s instructions. Confirm translation and recognition requirements separately.
France: For France, ask the recipient which form of the document it accepts and whether a translation is needed. Verify the applicable authentication route before submission.
Italy: For Italy, establish whether the request concerns document authentication, academic recognition or both. Confirm the receiving institution’s requirements for translations.
Canada: For Canada, distinguish an apostille request from credential evaluation or direct academic verification. Check the particular receiving organisation’s instructions.
Australia: For Australia, ask whether the recipient needs an original, certified copy or issuer verification. Authentication and professional or academic recognition are separate checks.
USA: For the USA, identify the specific receiving institution and its document rules. An employer, university and licensing board may ask for different evidence.
Europe: Europe is not a single document jurisdiction. Identify the specific country and receiving organisation before checking the authentication route.
Other: Start with the exact destination country and receiving organisation. We can help identify which official instructions to check for your document and purpose.
